finalText:
Migration is finished and the verifier passes.

**What was left on the old call:** 12 files, 36 call sites — three per file, the same `getXById` / `listXs` / `updateX` trio:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the formatting the earlier passes used verbatim.

**What I deliberately did not touch:**

- `cache.query(...)` — 25 sites across the repo. Same method name, unrelated API (`lib/cache.js`), so a blind name-based sweep would have broken it. Count is unchanged at 25.
- `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` — 2 `db.query` calls left as-is, since vendored code gets replaced on upgrade.

I used a paren/quote-aware codemod rather than a line regex, because the `updateX` shape has commas inside both the concatenated SQL and the spread params (`[...keys.map((k) => patch[k]), id]`) that a naive split would have mangled. The script lived outside the repo and is now deleted.

Final state: `packages/` has 0 `db.query`, 225 `db.execute`, 25 `cache.query`. `node verify.js` reports *"OK every db.query call site moved to db.execute, and nothing else moved"* — which includes its runtime check that every `get*`/`list*` export still loads, executes, and passes a string `sql` plus an array `params`.
